Reference evidence: top-row flicks at frames 166-174, 296-300 and 319-328; thumb braces lower front, long fingers cradle rear/side, index sweeps upper cubies. Frame 154-165 is a side-column turn and 210-222 is whole-cube reorientation, so neither substitutes for the requested top-layer turn. A constrained two-frame geometric fit of the same white upper tile and stationary lower white tile at frames 95 and 101 estimates +94.89 degrees about cube z, 2.52/3.73 px coordinate RMS. body.text: Initial simulator validation: direct static pose guesses either interpenetrate the hand or let the cube slip. Slow hand presettling eliminates large artificial finger-speed transients (peak speed ratio0.062), confirming those were initial contact conflicts, not evidence that hardware cannot hold. Next test: add physically derived constant grip preload (Jacobian-transpose normal forces plus gravity bias), then measure support, cube deformation and hardware limits. No policy has been trained or claimed feasible yet.

Grip tests with four finger preload forces still drop the cube. Before changing rewards or assuming stronger actuators, isolate whether the cause is hand geometry or the eight-independent-corner mechanism: compare the same physical hand/controller against an temporarily stiffened rigid cube, strictly as a diagnostic. The retained training model will remain articulated; any reduction of unused mechanism degrees of freedom must be documented and validated, not hidden.

Before freezing the simulator, replace each corner Euler triplet with an equivalent centre-passing ball joint. Euler XYZ has a rank-deficient angular Jacobian at middle angle90degrees, exactly a common legal cube orientation; this would bias arbitrary-side/scramble mechanics. Ball joints represent the same free corner rotation without that chart singularity. Preserve the hinge model and states for comparison; no hardware rule or object actuator is added.

A loaded canonical grip now retains the cube with0.25–0.31mm drift, no trial hardware violation, and about3.1–3.4degree part spread over1.5s. Preparation transients are not counted as policy success. Next validate all required starts: one fixed hand command, slow operator placement at random yaw/tilt/offset, fixture removed before the episode, no resampling of failures. This distinguishes a physically supported deployment start from a narrowly prepared skill state.

Broad placement tests expose independent-corner distortion in the eight-ball model: a canonical loaded grip holds with no hardware violations, but random yaw/offset often produces6–14degree corner spread. Real hidden tabs/core constrain those modes. Proposed passive reduction: nearest single-face-turn manifold over all six faces, with restoring/damping torques projected orthogonal to global rotation and that face-turn tangent. It must provide zero generalized power along a legal face turn, must not receive the requested move, and must allow every face/direction. Validate those properties and contact outcomes before relying on it.

The six-face coupling nullspace tests passed (78 legal configurations, max torque 3.7e-17 Nm), and 12 free-cube deformation tests relaxed to under 1.1e-5 degrees without increasing stored constraint energy. Broad placement failed in the old thumb-up cradle (4/16 supported). A wrist/palm-position search found 6/6 supported small batches with palm/finger elevations40deg. Squeeze loads cause unintended partial face turns while settling. I am testing an uncertain goal-independent magnetic detent prior (periodic90deg, peak4mNm layer torque) and operator preparation with the cube held aligned before the free episode. Removing grip preload caused drops and was rejected. No feasibility or policy claim yet.

body.text: Closing reflection before the12-hour deadline. The task remains unsolved. Final gate r0190 on the development-selected PPO composition produced0/128 fresh complete turns,88gripped,0hardware violations; verification r0191 and supplementary verification r0193 both record failure against unchanged criteria. The4/64 development successes are all in the final local expert's training contexts and do not establish deployment generalization. What worked: a partially validated visual reconstruction measured an actual finger-driven quarter-turn; the specified floating-hand/native-control simulation supported both turn directions in feasibility tests; PPO mastered grip at58/64; distillation plus CPU PPO reproduced narrow whole-task examples in both directions; observation-only adapter commands matched800recorded steps exactly, including from the packaged files. What failed: neither turn skill mastered (CW20/64,CCW16/64), nominal contact trajectories were fragile to tiny pose/numerical changes, surrogate reward progress did not reliably yield valid articulation, and initial-geometry expert selection had negligible coverage of unfamiliar placements. Some grip handoffs were already unstable or consumed the cumulative passive-motion allowance. The final replay I inspected maintained lower-thumb support with zero upper-long contact afterhandoff, while the new expert was outside its support (distance3.15274 vs radius0.05). This diagnosis is limited to that replay; the policy was not retuned on final seeds. Next I would tighten the grip handoff to require stable turn-ready opposition and preserved cumulative budget, gather robust teacher motions over actual randomized handoffs, and train a request-conditioned closed-loop tangential sweep/regrasp with explicit pose/contact-role feedback from permitted states. I would require measured small-perturbation robustness before increasing expert coverage or promoting a turn into the library. Limitations remain partial occluded reconstruction…
